security_invariant: A URL authority used for authorization must preserve the same host and port meaning through parsing and serialization.
attacker_controlled_source: A URL string whose authority contains a trailing empty port delimiter.
missing_or_incorrect_control: The port rule requires at least one digit, so it does not consume an empty port delimiter and leaves the colon in host and hostname.
sensitive_operation: Consumers compare parsed host, hostname, origin, or href values at an authorization or allowlist boundary before using the serialized URL.
vulnerable_behavior: The parser and serializer disagree about a trailing empty port, allowing an invalid or ambiguous authority to be normalized into a different URL representation across the security decision and later use.
fixed_behavior: The parser consumes an empty port delimiter, and the serializer preserves any remaining trailing colon so an invalid URL is not made valid.
root_cause: Empty-port authorities are parsed and serialized inconsistently: the port regex accepts digits only, while host serialization does not preserve a remaining trailing colon. This creates URL authority confusion at authorization and allowlist boundaries.
required_evidence: Trace an empty-port authority through the port, host, and hostname rules.
Compare the parsed origin and serialized href before and after the fix.
Show where a consumer can authorize one URL representation and use another.
refutation_checks: Check whether the consuming authorization layer reparses with one canonical parser.
Check whether empty or non-numeric ports are rejected before any security decision.
